title: George Wettling's tuning, taste and humor
summary: Leeman admires Wettling's tuned drums and humorous solos, and recalls following him in Shaw's first band and battles of music with Berigan's band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: George Wettling, another great Chicago drummer, with superb taste, he got a musical sound in tuning his drums, he was well studied in drum instruction, and a most exciting soloist -- his solos also had a great deal of humor in them, technique -- and we were wonderful friends, and I lean towards

many of his musical approaches as my own career continued. George and I first knew, after I followed him in Shaw's first big band, and I would find him at Nick's in the Village, in 1936, and he was with Bunny Berigan's first band, and one-nighters through New England, we had battles of music with them, and a battle of music in those days was two bands that was promoted by the ballroom, and the bookers, two bands in the same ballroom taking alternative sets, and let the people decide which band they liked best. I don't know what it proved, but it was interesting.
